div.head: III Atr 13.4
div.ab: ⁊ se ðe ofer ðæt láde geþafie oððe se þe hy sylle, gilde VI healfmarc.
Et qui super id ladam prorogat uel qui dat, reddat sex dimidiam marcam.
⁊ se ðe ofer ðæt láde geþafie oððe se þe hy sylle, gilde VI healfmarc.
Und wer trotzdem [dem Gegner] Reinigungsbeweis gestattet oder wer ihn [ihm] ablegt, büsse 6 Halbmark.
And whoever, despite that, allows [his opponent] proof by clearing, or whoever gives it [to him], let him pay 6 half-marks.
And he who subsequently permits a man to clear himself [of a transaction], and [likewise] he who offers to clear himself shall pay 6 half-marks.
And he who in spite of it admits exculpation, or he who offers it, is to pay six half-marks.

note.seg: Q scheint (durch ofer verführt?) an ein Hinauszögern zu denken, oder sagt er prorogare im Sinne von rogare: ‘fordern’?—Vom ‘Zulassen’ der Beweisart durch den Kläger sagt þafian auch Duns 2, 1. Dieser gestaltet den Beweis (s. d. Gl 4f.) auch sonst

Q seems (misled by ofer?) to be thinking of a postponement, or does he use prorogare in the sense of rogare, ‘demand’? — þafian is also used in Duns 2, 1 of the plaintiff’s ‘allowing’ the mode of proof. The plaintiff determines the form of the proof (see that word in Gl 4f.) in other cases too
gesellan steht synonym mit gelæstan, fullfremman, und sellan heisst ‘leisten, erbringen’ vom Eide auch sonst (s. Wb); lade gelecgean, gedon belegt Toller 605
gesellan is used synonymously with gelæstan, fullfremman, and sellan means ‘perform, render’ of the oath elsewhere too (see Wb); Toller 605 attests lade gelecgean, gedon
Liebermann takes the phrase to mean ‘in spite of that.’ BT. p. 605, s.v. lad ii., translate: ‘He that admits or he that offers purgation after that shall pay 6 half-marks.’
